claims.text: DFT simulations can facilitate production of noble metal–based HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks with precise atomic control.
DFT can identify stable NM-HEA configurations that are useful for nanoframework production.
The initial NM-HEAs are in a disordered, non-equilibrium state.
Applying DFT can predict stable NM-HEA configurations in a three-dimensional nanoframework structure.
Suitable DFT parameters include GGA-PBE, a 500 eV plane-wave cutoff, and a 5x5x5 Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid.
DFT-predicted stable configurations can serve as templates for synthesizing NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
DFT simulations provide insight into the thermodynamic stability of NM-HEAs.
DFT simulations provide insight into the electronic properties of NM-HEAs.
Thermodynamic and electronic-property predictions permit identification of optimal NM-HEA compositions and structures for forming three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
DFT-guided production will increase the yield of NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks by 25% relative to traditional synthesis.
DFT-guided production will provide precise atomic control of the resulting nanoframeworks.
HRTEM and XPS can measure the claimed yield and precise atomic control.
Candidate stable configurations must have formation energies within 0.1 eV/atom of the most stable DFT configuration.
The choice of exchange-correlation functional and other simulation parameters can limit DFT accuracy.
Errors arising from DFT parameter choices could affect the predicted stable configurations and the resulting nanoframework yield.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 25% yield increase, but the falsification rule accepts any increase of at least 15%. An observed increase between 15% and 25% would fail to support the stated quantitative prediction while not falsifying it under the proposed rule.
